handback.title: A settings file picks each role's agent and model
handback.summary: One settings file per repo says which subscription and model the planner, worker and reviewer use; Kimi first, then Codex.
handback.feature: Each role runs on the subscription and model the owner sets in one file. Stories: setup, the file, one agent interface, Kimi, Codex, rules later.

stories.title: Setup gathers and stores a subscription's inputs
stories.user_story: The owner adds a subscription by giving its inputs once; setup puts each where runs find it.
stories.context: The owner already did this by hand once for Kimi (their comment of 2026-10-15): Kimi Code CLI 2.2.0 installed, signed in with `kimi login --region global` through a browser device code, and one unattended run with `kimi -p ... --output-format stream-json` fixed a bug. Plan: Max, model access K3, default model kimi-for-coding. Today the only agent key is the `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` secret read in `.github/workflows/agent.yml`; the owner allowed workflow changes and new keys (answer 2). Setup writes the subscriptions part of the settings file story 2 defines; the format is fixed in story 2's context, so both can be built against it. Repo setup today lives in `dokima/audit.py` (the Setup issue, `setup_body`).

acceptance_criteria.text: Setup lists each input a subscription needs: membership, region, sign-in or key, and model.
acceptance_criteria.words: grabbing the inputs a user needs for a subscription (membership, region, sign-in or key, model)

acceptance_criteria.text: Setup puts each given input in place: the key as a repo secret, the rest in the settings file.

stories.title: One settings file per repo names subscriptions and roles
stories.user_story: The owner sets each role's subscription and model in one structured file in the repo.
stories.context: No settings file exists today; the model is fixed once for every role (`.github/workflows/agent.yml` line 59, `MODEL: claude-opus-5-5`). The owner fixed the path and shape: `.dokima/agents.yml`, with `subscriptions` (each: agent, key) and `roles` (planner, worker, reviewer: subscription and model). The key field names the secret holding the key, never the key itself. The repo adds no dependencies and PyYAML is not installed, so the file needs a small reader of its own; `tests/test_start.py` `load_yaml` shows a subset reader already in the tests. Its edge cases: a role left out of the file runs as today; an unknown subscription or agent name stops the run before the agent starts, naming the bad name.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each repo keeps its agent settings in one YAML file in its Dokima folder.
The file lists subscriptions, each naming its agent and the secret holding its key.
The file gives the planner, the worker and the reviewer each a subscription and a model.
acceptance_criteria.words: `roles` (planner, worker, reviewer: which subscription and model)

acceptance_criteria.text: A role may name any model its agent takes; Dokima keeps no list of allowed models.
acceptance_criteria.words: Any agent, any model: planner, worker and reviewer each pick theirs.

non_functional.text: Subscriptions and roles sit in their own sections, so other settings can join the file later.
non_functional.why: The owner expects the file to hold other settings later.
non_functional.words: Later it may expand into other settings.

stories.title: Every run starts its agent through one interface
stories.user_story: Each role runs on the subscription and model the file gives it, and Claude Code works as today.
stories.context: Today `.github/workflows/agent.yml` installs Claude Code and runs `claude -p ... --model "$MODEL"` for every role, then fails the run when the session logs name another model (line 565; `dokima/agent_records.py` `models_used`, `run_report` and `transcript` read Claude's logs under `~/.claude/projects` and `claude.json`). One agent interface takes the role, prompt, model and output folder and starts the agent; Claude Code is its first adapter, with the same command, flags and record as today. The owner allowed the workflow change (answer 2). Edge cases from the plan review: no file runs as today (criterion 3.2); a role left out runs as today; an unknown subscription or agent stops the run before the agent starts, naming the bad name.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each run starts the agent of its role's subscription, with the model the file names.
acceptance_criteria.words: A settings file decides which agent and model each role uses, across subscriptions.

acceptance_criteria.text: With no settings file, every run starts Claude Code with today's model, as now.
Claude Code runs behind the one agent interface with the same command, record and stats as today.
acceptance_criteria.words: The file and one agent interface; Claude Code moves behind it unchanged.

acceptance_criteria.text: A model always runs in its own vendor's agent, never inside another vendor's agent.
acceptance_criteria.words: Each subscription runs its own vendor's agent with its own models: Kimi models in Kimi Code CLI, Codex in Codex CLI, Claude in Claude Code. No model runs inside another vendor's agent.

acceptance_criteria.text: Moving a role to another subscription takes one edit: that role's lines in the file.
acceptance_criteria.words: It exposes a simple interface for deciding the orchestration across subscriptions.

stories.title: A role can run on Kimi Code CLI
stories.user_story: The owner moves any role to Kimi by naming a Kimi subscription for it, and spends Kimi's credit.
stories.context: Built first of the new agents, as the owner ordered (answer 1: build Kimi first, to use up its credit). The owner's tested command: `kimi -p ... --output-format stream-json`, Kimi Code CLI 2.2.0, model kimi-for-coding. The adapter installs Kimi's command line in the workflow, passes the key from the subscription's secret, and reads Kimi's stream so the model check (`agent.yml` line 565) and the run's stats still work. Whether Dokima's own file moves every role to Kimi is the plan reviewer's open question to the owner.

acceptance_criteria.text: A role on a Kimi subscription runs in Kimi Code CLI, with the Kimi model the file names.

stories.title: A role can run on Codex CLI
stories.user_story: The owner moves any role to Codex by naming a Codex subscription for it.
stories.context: Built after Kimi, as the owner ordered ('Kimi first ... then Codex'). It reuses story 3's interface and story 4's pattern: install Codex's command line, pass its key from the subscription's secret, read its logs for the model check and stats. Open issue 39 stays the general rule for adapters (answer 3).

acceptance_criteria.text: A role on a Codex subscription runs in Codex CLI, with the Codex model the file names.

stories.title: Rules across subscriptions live in the settings file
stories.user_story: The owner writes rules across subscriptions in the same settings file.
stories.context: The owner marked this story 'Later' and named no rule yet; see the question to the owner. Its planner asks which rules before planning.

acceptance_criteria.text: Rules across subscriptions are written in the same settings file as the roles.
acceptance_criteria.words: Later: rules across subscriptions, in the same file.

raises.label: Which later rules?
raises.text: Which rules across subscriptions does the later story need? The plan keeps it as a story until you name them.
raises.evidence: The owner's comment lists '5. Later: rules across subscriptions, in the same file.' and names no rule.

answers.why: No file or a left-out role runs as today; an unknown name stops the run, naming it.
